newsitem.title: USA: INDIA 96/97 COTTON EXPORTS 1.45 MLN BALES -ATTACHE.
newsitem.headline: INDIA 96/97 COTTON EXPORTS 1.45 MLN BALES -ATTACHE.

text.p: Cotton exports from India have been stronger than anticipated and now are expected at 1.45 million bales in 1996/97, the U.S. agricultural attache in New Delhi said in a report released Wednesday.
Exports through July 23 totaled 1.3 million bales, including 395,645 bales of spillover from 1995/96 export quotas, the attache said. Bales weigh 480 lbs.

"Market arrivals from the 1996 cotton crop continue to exceed expectations as farmers and traders have begun selling their cotton stocks in anticipation of a good 1997 harvest and weak prices," the attache wrote.
"The 1996 cotton crop is now estimated at 16.8 million bales and 1996/97 exports are estimated higher at 1.45 million bales.
"Monsoon rains have been generally good in cotton growing areas and planting is nearing completion in central and southern India; the crop is progressing well at this stage."
The new crop was estimated at 12.1 million bales, unchanged from an earlier estimate.
